Jaison Drops Poki Mini Bike With One-Touch and Customizable Wheelie Mode – Has a $1,800 Price Tag
24 photos
Photo: Jaison Bike
The electric mini bike industry has really been taking off lately, and in the wave of rides we can find the fresh Poki from Jaison. It’s not an e-bike, but rather, a full-blown mini bike which really has the proper feeling to it. Time to take a look at what's in store here.
Jaison Bike is one of those teams that caught the electrification wave and in it, grew to sell their mobility solutions worldwide. Ive seen them on the streets of the US and as far as Europe. Well, they just dropped word of the newest addition to their family: the Poki.
Now, what makes this one so special is that Jaison broke away from the traditional e-bikes that we’re used to from them, and instead, brings to life a pedal-less machine that relies on nothing other than throttle to move around. Just kick back and enjoy the ride, literally. To do that, there are a few systems to do so, and not just throttle; we’ll get to all that.
Photo: Jaison Bike First off, we have ourselves the overall design of the Poki, completed from what I can only guess is steel because this thing weighs 137.5 lbs (62.3 kg). Sure, the motor and battery are to blame for the heavy weight, but that only goes so far, so I have my money on steel tubes for the rest of the weight.
Speaking of the battery and motor, at its core, the Poki is built upon a 60 V ecosystem, granting us access to some rather punchy acceleration. Couple that with a motor that peaks at a whopping 6,720 W, or a bit over 9 hp, so yes, I can see the minibike vibes for sure.
According to Jaison’s website, the 60 V and 9 hp amount to a top speed of as much as 50 mph (80 kph), although some riders have mentioned that they’ve been able to go beyond that number. A 60 V and 80 A controller is there managing all the flow of juice. A “tiny menace” indeed.
Photo: Jaison Bike Why so much spunk out of a product that costs us just $1,800 (€1,600)? Aside from the thrill and fun factor, the power the Poki brings to the table has purpose: stunts .
Stunts? Yes, stunts, and ones that are controlled via hardware and software in order to assist new and experienced riders to stay in a wheelie position, one that you can even set through an app so that you can grow with the Poki as you get better at keeping your balance.
Some riders go nuts with this thing locked into a wheelie angle. Anywhere from 15 degrees to 60 degrees is on the menu here, making for some wicked Instagram videos and clips.
Photo: Jaison Bike What is neat is that we can tune acceleration, how much the brakes kick in, and much more, all with the goal of helping you tune your ride to your liking and above all, abilities. This trait of the Poki is not to be overlooked; not all minibikes out there have it.
In the range department, the Poki surprised once again, showcasing a peak range of as much as 60 miles (96.5 km) on a single charge (30 Ah battery), but best of all, in just 3 hours, it can reach an 80% charge from 20% (with fast charger), so if you stay on top of charging, you should have no worries about range.
A few other traits that need to be considered are things like wheel size, suspension, and braking, all of which are as quirky as can be, but with purpose.
Photo: Jaison Bike In the suspension department, Jaison adds a rear setup, helping control your position on the bike as you wheelie around town, but at the front, there is no softness. What helps at the front as it comes down from being in the air for however long you held the wheelie are the wheels .
The plump, 13 cm (5.1 in) wheels sit on 6-inch rims and offer ample plushness as they land, but also as you roll around city streets. Be sure to check with local laws and regulations regarding mini bike use on your streets. The tires do appear as though they could also handle some off-road use too.
Photo: Jaison Bike The smaller rubbers also help bring the center of gravity lower to the ground, so if you do happen to take a spill while you’re out there, you shouldn’t be banging yourself up too much, even less if you’re wearing proper protective gear, which, at 50 mph top speeds, you clearly should.
Honestly, after covering this little pocket beast, I can say one thing: I'll be reaching out to Jaison to see if we can get our hands on one for a test, because of you ask me, this thing is pretty neat, especially at the $1,800 we’re being asked to drop on it. Keep in mind that this is a launch price and once the sale is done, it’s set to go back to $2,600; I really hope not.
Would you ride one of these babes around town?
